Hospital Course:

The patient presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain and was diagnosed with an ectopic pregnancy in the right adnexa. A laparoscopic right salpingectomy was performed, and regular obstetric follow-up was done for the intrauterine pregnancy. The baby was delivered via spontaneous vaginal delivery at term with no significant complications.

Discharge Instructions:

The patient is advised to continue with regular obstetric follow-up and to report any signs of complications immediately. Post-operative pain management should be done as prescribed. The patient should have a healthy diet and stay hydrated, and avoid strenuous physical activity until cleared by the obstetrician. 

Follow-up:

The patient is advised to schedule a follow-up appointment with their obstetrician as soon as possible.

text:
The principal diagnosis code is most likely **O00.11, Tubal pregnancy with intrauterine pregnancy** (ICD-10-AM).

This is a heterotopic pregnancy: an ectopic (right adnexal) pregnancy coexisting with a viable intrauterine pregnancy. The ectopic pregnancy occasioned the admission and was treated surgically with a laparoscopic right salpingectomy, so it is the principal diagnosis. The intrauterine pregnancy is captured by the "with intrauterine pregnancy" subcode.

Some caveats:
- The diagnosis sections are withheld, so the coder should confirm the admitting and discharge diagnoses in the full record.
- If the ectopic site were documented as abdominal or another site rather than tubal, a different O00 subcode would apply.
- The salpingectomy and the spontaneous vaginal delivery would be recorded as procedure codes and additional diagnosis codes, not as the principal diagnosis.
- Verify the code against the current ICD-10-AM/ACHI edition and local coding standards.
